title: fix: label README baseline fallback on days with no live picks
summary: On a day with no live picks, the README radar block in all three languages (README.md, README.en.md, README.ja.md) now explains the empty day the same way the frozen daily page does. readme_block in pairadar/render.py keeps the existing day heading and generated/window line. After them it adds the localized no-items sentence as a Markdown quote, then a bold label from the existing glossary baseline string, then the curated baseline table, evidence legend, reasons and links. Before this change, the baseline entries appeared under the day's heading, ranked and in the pick column, with no explanation. If there are no picks and no baseline, the block shows the no-items line and an empty table header without raising. Days with picks keep the previous rendering. docs/METHODOLOGY.md describes the empty-day README behavior. Checks run by the controller on candidate dfb3436 (base 047ef4a): before the change, the new test file failed 2 of 3 tests (the empty-day label test and the nothing-at-all test), which confirms the defect. After the change, rerender exited 0, the 3 tests in tests/test_feature_b41f745004f1.py passed, and the full suite of 484 tests passed.
usage:
Prerequisites: a checkout of this repository, Python 3 and the repository root as the working directory. The pipeline uses only the standard library. No sample input file is needed: the feature tests build a synthetic in-memory ctx with an empty picked list and use the repository's curated baseline. These are the same commands the controller ran:

python -m pairadar --rerender --no-readme
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_feature_b41f745004f1.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests

The first command re-renders the current published snapshot without touching the README files. In the controller run it reported 8 published picks for 2026-10-04, so it exercises the normal-day path. The second command checks the empty-day behavior in zh, en and ja. In each language, the block must contain the line '> ' plus the glossary no_items sentence after the generated/window line, then '**' plus the glossary baseline label before the table header. Every baseline title must still be in the table. The command also checks that a day with picks has neither line, and that a day with no picks and no baseline renders without error. On a real empty day, the normal scheduled run regenerates the README blocks with this labelling.
limitations: Only the README radar block's empty-picks case changed. These are unchanged: the landing-site cards (pairadar/site.py), the banner, the charts, partly filled days (fewer picks than the maximum), selection thresholds, per-lane caps and the 30-day duplicate window. The wording reuses the existing no_items and baseline glossary strings, and no new translations were added. The evidence is string assertions on synthetic ctx data and a rerender of a snapshot with picks. The controller's receipts do not include a live empty day, and no browser or visual review of how GitHub renders the new quote and label was done for this feature. Passing tests show the specified structure, not the readability of the rendered page. The normal-day test passed both before and after the change, but byte-identity was only checked for the cases the tests cover. The issue #73 EgoScale figure in data/baseline.json is still uncorrected and is out of scope for this lane.
upgrade: There are no data, schema, configuration or dependency changes. After the upgrade, the next scheduled run or rerender that writes READMEs regenerates the radar blocks between the existing RADAR markers. Saved snapshots, feeds, weekly pages and frozen daily pages are not rewritten. To roll back, revert commit dfb3436. The next README-writing run then restores the previous unlabeled baseline fallback. Nothing else needs to be migrated or cleaned up.

title: require a reviewed Git source commit when opening a skill over MCP
summary:
MCP open_skill accepts a new optional input, expected_source_commit. Set it to the receipt.source_commit value from an earlier load, and the skill is delivered only while the Git-source checkout HEAD is still that commit. When the field is supplied, the checks run in this order: format (40 lowercase hex characters, enforced by the input schema), Git-source origin, the existing expected_sha256 and expected_bundle_sha256 checks (wording unchanged), a provable commit from the existing sourceCommit() probe, and an exact match. Any failure returns isError true with an actionable message and no instruction text or receipt. A mismatch names both the expected and the found commit. A rejected digest still runs no Git command. Calls that omit the field behave as before. tools/list shows the field as optional.

Results from the controller's runs on commit 6a40534. These are the controller's executions, not mine. With the new test file run against the base code, 4 of its 6 tests failed: the moved-checkout, unprovable-commit, malformed-pin/non-Git and tools/list tests. The 2 tests that check unchanged existing behavior passed. On the candidate, every check passed: pnpm run build, the feature test (6 tests), pnpm run check (25 test files, 251 tests), pnpm run showcase:build and pnpm run showcase:check.

The prior review finding is addressed. As the logged test source shows, the malformed-pin test reads the resolved callTool result directly and asserts both isError true and the schema message (must be a full 40-character lowercase Git commit). It no longer wraps the call in a try/catch that would turn thrown errors into isError.
usage:
Prerequisites: git, Node and pnpm, this package built with pnpm run build, and an MCP client connected to the skills-anywhere MCP server.

1. Create a synthetic sample Git source (demo data only):
mkdir -p /tmp/demo-skills/robot-reel-review && cd /tmp/demo-skills && git init -q && printf -- '---\nname: robot-reel-review\ndescription: Synthetic demo skill\n---\n\nReview the robot reel.\n' > robot-reel-review/SKILL.md && git add -A && git -c user.name=demo -c user.email=demo@example.com commit -qm initial

2. Manual step: register /tmp/demo-skills as a Git source using the source configuration described in README.md, then let the server sync it into its source cache. The config syntax is not repeated here.

3. Over MCP, call open_skill with {"name": "robot-reel-review"} and record structuredContent.receipt.source_commit, a 40-character lowercase hex value.

4. On later loads, call open_skill with {"name": "robot-reel-review", "expected_source_commit": "<that value>"}. The result is the same content, and receipt.source_commit equals the pin.

5. Commit a change in /tmp/demo-skills and sync it into the cache. Repeat the pinned call. The result has isError true and reads: Git source commit changed for "robot-reel-review": expected <old>, found <new>; review the change before updating expected_source_commit.

6. After you review the new revision, replace the pin with the found commit.

See docs/VERIFIED-LOADS.md, section on requiring the reviewed source commit.
limitations:
Scope: the standalone MCP open_skill tool, for skills from configured Git sources only. The dsh provider skill tool, skill:// resources and the CLI are unchanged.

What the pin proves: it proves the checkout HEAD, not the absence of uncommitted or untracked files. Combine it with expected_bundle_sha256 to cover directory contents. Files can still change after a load.

Not included: automatic re-sync, rollback, and signature or author verification.

Test coverage: the feature tests use synthetic local Git repositories and an in-process MCP client. They confirm that malformed pins come back as an isError result with this repository's pinned MCP SDK. Other SDK versions or clients were not exercised, and no branded client application was tested. Clients that cache tool schemas may need to reconnect before they see the new field.

UI and browser evidence: this feature has no UI. The controller's showcase:check run passed the existing showcase browser regression checks (desktop/mobile, keyboard tabs, offline and others). Those checks cover the showcase site, not this feature, and no visual review of this feature applies. Passing tests do not establish behavior beyond the tested cases.
upgrade:
Upgrade: this is an additive, optional input. Existing calls, receipts, lock files and cache layout are unchanged, so no migration is needed.

Rollback: stop sending expected_source_commit or downgrade the package. Pinned calls sent to an older server are not enforced, because the field is not in that schema, so do not rely on the pin after a downgrade.

Adopting a new revision: review it, then update the pin to the commit named in the mismatch error or to the receipt.source_commit from a fresh unpinned load.

title: fix: fail the diff gate when the baseline run did not finish
summary:
evalarc diff and the GitHub Action now fail the gate (exit 1) when the baseline run did not finish. Before this change, an Inspect baseline log whose status was not success could pass. Checks missing from it were classified as 'added', and 'added' never blocks. Change classification, counts and blocking rules are unchanged. When the baseline is incomplete, diff.json gains "baseline_incomplete": true and gate_passed is false. When the baseline is complete, the key is left out, so those reports keep their previous content apart from created_at and version.

After the existing summary line, default stdout prints: 'The baseline run is incomplete (status error); N check(s) appear only in the current run and were not compared. Rerun the baseline to completion; the gate fails.'

summary.md and --markdown add a line below the table: 'The baseline run did not finish (status `error`); the gate fails because checks missing from it cannot be compared. N check(s) appear only in the current run. Rerun the baseline to completion.' The heading reads 'EvalArc: the baseline run is incomplete' only when there are no blocking changes and the current run finished. Otherwise it shows the existing blocking heading or 'the baseline and current runs are incomplete'.

index.html shows 'Gate failed' with the reason 'the baseline run is incomplete'. When there are no blocking rows, it says 'Rerun the baseline to completion and compare again.' evalarc verify recomputes the same result. docs/ci-gate.md and the README CI-gate paragraph document the rule.

The controller ran the checks; the author did not run anything. On base commit dc848cc, tests/test_feature_f107c0a41d3a.py failed (5 failed, 1 passed), which confirms the gap. On candidate bc6089b, these all exited 0: the feature test, the full pytest suite, ruff check, ruff format --check, scripts/build_site.py and node scripts/check_site.cjs.
usage:
Prerequisites: evalarc at commit bc6089b or later is installed (for example, pip install -e . in a repository checkout), and the commands run from the repository root, which contains examples/results-diff/inspect/baseline.json.

Step 1. Create a SYNTHETIC unfinished baseline. This copies the bundled example log, sets status to error and removes the refund-duplicate samples, imitating an interrupted Inspect run:

python - <<'EOF'
import json, pathlib
src = pathlib.Path('examples/results-diff/inspect/baseline.json')
log = json.loads(src.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
log['status'] = 'error'
log['samples'] = [s for s in log['samples'] if s.get('id') != 'refund-duplicate']
pathlib.Path('/tmp/unfinished-baseline.json').write_text(json.dumps(log), encoding='utf-8')
EOF

Step 2. Compare it with the finished example log. The --output folder must not already exist:

evalarc diff /tmp/unfinished-baseline.json examples/results-diff/inspect/baseline.json --output /tmp/diff-review --markdown /tmp/summary.md
echo "exit: $?"

Expected results:
- Exit code 1.
- Stdout contains 'The baseline run is incomplete (status error); 2 check(s) appear only in the current run and were not compared. Rerun the baseline to completion; the gate fails.'
- /tmp/diff-review/diff.json contains "baseline_incomplete": true.
- /tmp/diff-review/index.html shows 'Gate failed', 'the baseline run is incomplete' and 'Rerun the baseline to completion and compare again.'
- /tmp/summary.md contains 'The baseline run did not finish (status `error`)'.

Step 3. Confirm the saved folder recomputes:

evalarc verify /tmp/diff-review --json

In CI: evalarc diff evals/baseline.json results/current.json --output runs/diff-review --markdown "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY". If this fails because the baseline is incomplete, regenerate a finished baseline (for example, rerun inspect eval to completion) and compare again.
limitations:
Scope: one gate rule for an unfinished baseline. It appears in the existing terminal, JSON, Markdown and HTML outputs. docs/ci-gate.md and the README CI-gate paragraph state the rule. The translated docs, docs/ci-gate.zh-CN.md and README.zh-CN.md, are not updated with it. Not included: new flags or override modes, relabelling 'added' checks, reconstructing missing samples, duplicate-ID or malformed-record handling, and other EA-02 corpus items.

The rule depends on the run status that the export records. Exports with no run status, such as JUnit, are never marked incomplete, so the rule cannot fire for them.

The acceptance tests use synthetic fixtures derived from the bundled example Inspect log. No live or real interrupted Inspect run was tested. Passing tests show the specified behavior on those fixtures, not correctness across every Inspect version or log variant.

The new HTML text is covered by string assertions only. The controller's node scripts/check_site.cjs run passed the existing showcase browser regression checks (keyboard, links and downloads at 1440, 390 and 320 px widths). Those checks do not exercise this feature's diff-report banner. No screenshot or visual review of the new state was performed.

Behavior change: pipelines that passed with an interrupted baseline now fail. Report folders saved by 0.17.2 with an incomplete baseline will show a recomputation mismatch in evalarc verify, because they recorded a pass. Folders with finished baselines are unaffected.
upgrade:
To upgrade, install the patch release that contains commit bc6089b (the CHANGELOG 0.17.3 entry) or pin the matching Action tag. No migration is needed, and existing result files and report folders are not modified. The new diff.json key appears only when the baseline is incomplete, so schema-v1 consumers keep working.

Expect pipelines that compared against an interrupted baseline to start exiting 1. The intended fix is to regenerate a finished baseline.

To roll back, pin noteflowai/evalarc@v0.17.2 or evalarc==0.17.2. Nothing is rewritten, so rollback loses no data. However, rollback restores the old behavior, in which an unfinished baseline can pass the gate.

If you rerun evalarc verify on a folder saved by 0.17.2 with an incomplete baseline, expect a mismatch. Regenerate that report with the new version instead of editing it.

title: record the Git source commit in MCP open_skill receipts
summary: On candidate commit 59390b7, a successful MCP open_skill call that passes its expected_sha256 and expected_bundle_sha256 checks now returns structuredContent.receipt.source_commit. For a skill from a Git source, it is the 40-character lowercase HEAD SHA of that source's cache checkout at load time. For agent directories, plugin marketplaces and extra local directories it is null, and no Git command runs for them. For a Git source whose commit cannot be proven, it is also null and the server logs one 'skills-anywhere: source commit unavailable for <name>: <reason>' warning. That covers Git missing or failing, a timeout, or a work tree with no .git of its own or one outside the cache. The load still returns unchanged content in that case. Git runs without a shell and with GIT_* variables removed. Discovery stops at the cache directory, so the commit of an enclosing repository is never reported. Rejected loads throw their existing errors before any Git lookup. The advertised outputSchema declares source_commit. The schema string stays skills-anywhere-load-1. These are unchanged: loadReceipt(), LoadReceipt, OpenedSkill, the exported openSkill(), dsh provider and tool receipts, skill:// resources and rendered text. Controller-run checks on 59390b7: an acceptance-before run failed 3/3 feature tests because the receipt had only 11 fields. After the change, pnpm run build passed. tests/test_feature_ea6b51801ed9.test.ts passed. pnpm run check passed, and its log shows 24 test files and 245 tests passing. pnpm run showcase:build and pnpm run showcase:check also passed.
usage:
Prerequisites: Node.js with npx, and git. All data below is a synthetic demo. This sequence is a manual example and the controller did not run it.

mkdir -p my-skills-repo/my-skill
cat > my-skills-repo/my-skill/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: my-skill
description: Synthetic demo skill
---
Demo instructions v1.
EOF
git -C my-skills-repo init -q -b main
git -C my-skills-repo add -A
git -C my-skills-repo -c user.name=demo -c user.email=demo@example.invalid commit -qm v1
export DSH_HOME="$PWD/demo-dsh"
npx dsh-skills-anywhere add ./my-skills-repo
npx dsh-skills-anywhere sync
open_demo() {
  (printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"demo","version":"0"}}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"open_skill","arguments":{"name":"my-skill"}}}'; sleep 3) | npx dsh-skills-anywhere mcp
}
open_demo
git -C my-skills-repo rev-parse HEAD

The id 2 response's structuredContent.receipt.source_commit should match the printed SHA. Next, edit SKILL.md, commit v2, run sync and call open_demo again: source_commit shows the new HEAD. Then run git -C my-skills-repo reset --hard HEAD~1, sync again and call open_demo: the v1 SHA comes back. Skills from agent directories show source_commit null.
limitations:
Scope: this adds one nullable field to MCP open_skill receipts only. The exported openSkill() and dsh receipts do not include it. There is no expected_commit argument, no check that the lock file agrees with the checkout, and no change to sync or clone. The field names only the cache checkout HEAD. Uncommitted edits in the cache are covered by skill_sha256 and bundle_sha256, not by this field. It does not verify signed commits, authenticate authors or prove instruction compliance. Each successful Git-source load starts one Git process with a 5-second bound. Strict consumers that reject unknown keys will see one new key.

Evidence: the passing tests use synthetic local file repositories in temporary directories. They do not cover remote hosts, every Git version or every platform. The usage sequence above was written by hand and was not executed by the controller. The controller ran the existing showcase browser regression checks (desktop/mobile iframe, keyboard tabs, offline and others) and they passed. This feature has no UI, and no screenshots were reviewed.
upgrade: Upgrade: install the version that contains commit 59390b7. Lock files, sources files, caches and saved receipts are read unchanged, and new MCP open_skill receipts gain source_commit. Rollback: reinstall the previous version. Receipts saved with source_commit stay valid JSON with the same schema string, and older consumers ignore the extra key. Nothing is migrated or deleted in either direction.

title: count final Bedrock chat failures by cause on the dashboard
summary:
Version 1.53.0 makes failed Amazon Bedrock chat calls visible on the existing admin dashboard. The Usage today card has a fourth metric, Failed requests. The seven-day usage panel has one line, for example 'Failed chat requests, last 7 days: 4. Throttled 3, access denied 1.' When there are none it reads 'No failed chat requests recorded in the last 7 days.' The line also appears in the existing empty state. A site where every call fails no longer looks like a quiet site.

A failure is counted once per handle_chat_message() or stream_chat_message() call, only if that call sent at least one Bedrock HTTP request and still returned an error after fallback and Converse adaptation retries. AI_Chat_Bedrock_Usage::classify_failure() sorts it into one of six categories using the HTTP status and the plugin error code: throttled (429), access_denied (401/403), validation (400), unavailable (5xx), network (status 0 with aicfab_unreachable or aicfab_stream_interrupted) or other.

Some cases are not counted:
- Missing credentials, an invalid region or model, the daily limit, and encoding errors. None of these send a request.
- Retries that later succeeded.
- Stopped streams.

Only per-day category counts are stored in the existing ai_chat_bedrock_usage option. No message, prompt, output, error text, user ID or IP is kept. Requests, tokens, per-model counts and the daily cap still count successful invocations only.

Controller-run checks on commit d1da36b:
- Before the change, the new test failed with exit 255 (undefined classify_failure) on the base code.
- tests/test_feature_364f48c382c4.php passed with assertions enabled.
- bin/prerelease.sh passed: 47 suites including usage.php and admin-ux.php, phpcs clean, and versions all 1.53.0.
- tests/tooling.php passed.
- bin/build-package.py built the 1.53.0 zip.

The stream_chat_message() return-path check that failed in the prior review now passes.
usage:
Dashboard (no setup): sign in to wp-admin as a user with manage_options and open admin.php?page=ai-chat-for-amazon-bedrock. Read Failed requests in the Usage today card, then the 'Failed chat requests, last 7 days' line in the seven-day usage panel.

Expected behavior: with a fallback model set, if the primary model returns 429 and the fallback returns 500, the call sends 2 requests. Failed requests rises by 1, and the line reads 'Failed chat requests, last 7 days: 1. Throttled 1.'

Synthetic example. Prerequisites: WP-CLI on a staging site with 1.53.0 active. This writes a real counter to that site's usage option, so do not run it in production. No input file is needed.

wp eval 'AI_Chat_Bedrock_Usage::record_failure( "throttled" ); print_r( AI_Chat_Bedrock_Usage::failure_totals( 7 ) );'

This prints total 1 (or one more than before) with by_category keys in the order throttled, access_denied, validation, unavailable, network, other. Reload the dashboard to see the line. To clear it, use the plugin's usage reset, which also clears request and token counters.

Regression test (prerequisites: PHP CLI and a repository checkout; uses synthetic stubbed Bedrock responses and needs no AWS access):

php -d zend.assertions=1 -d assert.exception=1 tests/test_feature_364f48c382c4.php

Expected output: 'All final-failure counter checks passed.' Full gate: bash bin/prerelease.sh --php /usr/bin/php
limitations:
Scope:
- Only chat calls through handle_chat_message() and stream_chat_message() are counted, including Diagnostics model tests, evaluations and content generation.
- Knowledge Bases, embeddings, MCP and AgentCore failures are not counted.
- Counts show what this plugin observed, not AWS service health.
- There are no failure rates, per-model or per-attempt counts, stored error messages, alerts or WP-CLI reporting.
- Failures from before the upgrade are not reconstructed.
- Categories come from a fixed status/code rule table. There is no AWS error-type classification, so anything unrecognized counts as other.

Test evidence:
- Every Bedrock response in the tests is a synthetic stub. Nothing reached AWS, so the tests show counting and classification logic, not behavior against live Bedrock.
- The streamed path is covered through the shared record_chat_outcome() method and a static source check, because cURL is not stubbed in this suite.
- Missing credentials are simulated by clearing client properties through reflection.
- In prerelease.sh, the official Plugin Check and the live WordPress integration step were skipped (no --wp-cli given).

Visual evidence:
- These receipts include no browser, screenshot, showcase or visual review of the new metric and line. public-script.test.mjs ran as a script test only.
- Layout, keyboard and responsive behavior rest on static review. The markup reuses existing aicfab-metric and aicfab-card-detail classes and adds no controls, scripts or style attributes.
- Passing tests do not establish visual quality.
upgrade:
Update to 1.53.0 as usual. There is no migration. Each day entry in the existing ai_chat_bedrock_usage option can gain an optional failures map of positive counts, and every day keeps its existing requests, tokens and models keys. Days recorded earlier read as zero failures. Failure counts follow the existing 30-day retention.

To roll back, reinstall the release you ran before 1.53.0. Its dashboard does not read the failures key. That release's handling of the extra key was not exercised in these checks. The design expects its prune() to rebuild each day from known keys and drop failures the next time it records a request, while keeping request and token counters. If in doubt, reset usage counters after rolling back. That reset clears failure, request and token counts together.

title: fix: name the first bad frame in LeRobot timeline errors
summary: robot-reel lerobot now names the first frame that breaks an episode's timeline. It still stops with exit status 2 and writes no output. Each message gives the dataset-relative data file, the episode and the first bad frame_index. There are five cases: a missing frame (with the next recorded frame_index), a repeated frame, an unexpected value (negative, null, NaN or non-numeric), a frame with no finite timestamp, and a timestamp that is not after the previous frame's (both values shown). Frame indices are now checked before the metadata length check, so a frame dropped mid-episode is reported as a gap instead of a count mismatch. A missing final frame keeps the old 'Episode metadata lists N frames but ... holds N-1' message. Every timeline message ends with 'Robot Reel does not reorder, fill or interpolate frames; repair or re-export the episode.' The accept/reject rule is unchanged, so float or bool frame_index columns equal to 0..length-1 are still accepted. docs/lerobot.md has a new 'Timeline errors' section. Controller results for commit f8e0c1e: before the fix, the new test file ran 10 tests on the base code with 5 failures (the old generic messages) and 5 skips. After the fix, one gated run passed the new test file, the full Python unittest suite, npm run check:js, node --test (52 of 52) and robot_reel.pages --write (0 files updated). I wrote this delivery text only; I did not run any of these checks myself.
usage:
Prerequisites: robot-reel with the lerobot extra (python -m pip install 'robot-reel[lerobot]'), which provides pyarrow. You also need a local LeRobot v2.1 dataset that you own, with per-episode parquet files, where episode 3 has at least 59 frames. This is a manual damage reproduction on a COPY of that dataset. The copy is a synthetic defect, not real collection damage.

cp -r ~/datasets/my_so101_run /tmp/rr_damaged
python - <<'EOF'
# Manual synthetic damage: drop frame_index 57 and leave meta/episodes.jsonl unchanged
import pyarrow.parquet as pq, pyarrow.compute as pc
p = '/tmp/rr_damaged/data/chunk-000/episode_000003.parquet'
t = pq.read_table(p)
pq.write_table(t.filter(pc.not_equal(t['frame_index'], 57)), p)
EOF
robot-reel lerobot /tmp/rr_damaged --episode 3 --output /tmp/rr_out; echo "exit $?"
# Expected: exit 2, no /tmp/rr_out files, and stderr:
# robot-reel lerobot: error: Episode 3 in data/chunk-000/episode_000003.parquet is missing frame_index 57 (next recorded frame_index is 58); frames must be 0..length-1 without gaps. Robot Reel does not reorder, fill or interpolate frames; repair or re-export the episode.

For a real damaged episode, filter it for the named frame_index, repair or re-export it, then rerun the same command. The repository's synthetic fixtures build their own temporary datasets, so no input file is needed to run them:
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_feature_4a9fd62e667c.py
limitations:
Only the frame_index and timestamp checks in read_episode changed. Only the first defect is reported. The numbers are frame_index values, not file row numbers. Nothing is repaired, reordered or interpolated. Timestamp columns with more than one value per frame keep the generic 'Timestamps are missing or not increasing' message. One order change: a missing timestamp or frame_index column is now reported before a metadata length mismatch.

All test fixtures are synthetic local v2.1 episodes with no cameras. The cases that ran use FakeReaderTimelineTest, a labeled stand-in for pyarrow.parquet that stores columns as JSON. That class exercises the error cases and the float64 frame_index export, --verify and --check-source path. It does not prove real parquet behavior. In the controller's pre-fix run, the 5 RealReaderTimelineTest cases (real parquet files) were skipped. The passing run used the same container image, and its log excerpt shows no skip counts, so no claim is made that the real-parquet cases ran. v2.0, v3.0 and Hub sources share the code path but have no dedicated fixtures. Passing tests show the specified messages for these fixtures; they do not show coverage of every real-world corruption.

The controller's node --test run passed 52 existing browser regression checks, including the desktop and mobile LeRobot replay checks. This feature changes no UI, and no visual review of it was performed. The RR-01 first-use observation with three independent users remains open.
upgrade: Patch-level upgrade. There are no schema, file-format or CLI flag changes, and the same episodes are accepted and rejected as before. Previously valid episodes, including float frame_index columns equal to 0..length-1, export with the same trace content. As in every release, the exporter.robot_reel version string changes, so the episode.json and index.html bytes and their manifest.json hashes differ from exports made by earlier versions. Existing exports still pass --verify, and --check-source against their dataset still passes. Rejected episodes still exit 2 and write nothing. Scripts that match the old exact strings 'Frame indices are not 0..length-1' or 'Timestamps are missing or not increasing' must switch to the new phrases, for example 'missing frame_index', 'repeats frame_index', 'no finite timestamp at frame_index' or 'does not reorder, fill or interpolate'. To roll back, reinstall the previous robot-reel version. No data migration is needed, and existing exported replays are unaffected.

title: claim-audit worksheet for recently published numeric claims (RA-01)
summary:
Adds python3 -m pairadar.claims, an offline, read-only command for the RA-01 claim review. It reads the published JSON Feed store (radar/feed.json by default). For each figure in the items[]._radar entries within the chosen window, it prints one row of a deterministic Markdown review sheet. The columns are #, day, evidence, claim, status, context, source and an empty review cell. Each status comes from distill.number_context applied to the stored text:
- quoted: the figure was found in the stored excerpt.
- title: the figure was found only in the title.
- no-excerpt: the stored excerpt is empty, as it is for baseline entries.
- unlocated: the figure is not in the stored title or truncated excerpt. Check the original source first.

The reference day is the newest valid entry date, not the system clock. The header gives the store path, reference day, days, total figures T, rows shown S and skipped entries K. title: fix: fail the diff gate when a check has fewer assessed attempts than the baseline
summary:
evalarc diff now has a blocking change kind, less_covered. A check gets it when the current run assessed fewer attempts than the baseline and the pass rate did not fall. A smaller sample can no longer be reported as improved or unchanged. For example, 2/2 to 1/1, 1/2 to 1/1, and 2/2 to 1/1 with one unassessed attempt are all less_covered, and the command exits 1. The existing kinds still take precedence. A lower pass rate is still reported as regressed or less_reliable. A check that passed before and now has zero assessed attempts is still unassessed. The CLI now reads its list of blocking kinds from BLOCKING, so it prints lines such as '  less_covered: cancel-pending / match'. With --output, diff.json keeps schema evalarc.results-diff.v1 and lists less_covered in counts and changes. summary.md shows a 'less covered' row with the baseline and current fractions, and the index.html row uses the existing failed styling. Comparisons where no check lost assessed attempts give the same results as before. docs/ci-gate.md and docs/ci-gate.zh-CN.md list less_covered in the change table.

Controller-executed checks on image sha256:3effc5c7...: On base commit e99bc9e, the new tests/test_feature_3412504c3ce6.py failed 6 of 15 tests. The trimmed comparison exited 0 and reported 'Unchanged: 16', which confirms the gap. On candidate commit d4a4afd, all of the following exited 0: that test file, the full pytest suite (including the unchanged tests/test_results_diff.py), ruff check, ruff format --check, scripts/build_site.py and node scripts/check_site.cjs. The earlier review finding that ruff format --check would fail is resolved by that passing run. I did not run these checks myself.
usage:
Prerequisites: an EvalArc checkout at commit d4a4afd or a release that contains it, Python 3.11+, and the package installed from the checkout. Run from the repository root:

python -m pip install -e .

Create a sample input. This is a synthetic, manually trimmed copy of the recorded Inspect example with the epoch-2 sample of cancel-pending removed. The status stays success.

python - <<'EOF'
import json, pathlib
src = pathlib.Path('examples/results-diff/inspect/baseline.json')
doc = json.loads(src.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
before = len(doc['samples'])
doc['samples'] = [s for s in doc['samples'] if not (s.get('id') == 'cancel-pending' and s.get('epoch') == 2)]
assert len(doc['samples']) == before - 1, 'expected to drop exactly one sample'
pathlib.Path('trimmed.json').write_text(json.dumps(doc), encoding='utf-8')
EOF

Compare it with the baseline. The output folder must not exist yet.

evalarc diff examples/results-diff/inspect/baseline.json trimmed.json --output trimmed-diff
echo "exit code: $?"

Expected result: the output includes the line '  less_covered: cancel-pending / match' and the exit code is 1. trimmed-diff/summary.md has a 'less covered' row for cancel-pending / match showing 2/2 against 1/1. trimmed-diff/diff.json has schema evalarc.results-diff.v1 and a less_covered count. trimmed-diff/index.html marks that row as failed. In CI, use the same command on your committed baseline and current log, for example: evalarc diff evals/baseline.json results/current.json --output evalarc-diff
limitations: Tests passing on fixtures do not show that the rule is right for every workflow. The rule compares raw assessed-attempt counts per check. It has no statistical tolerance, flag or opt-out, so any drop in assessed attempts blocks, even one lost attempt out of many. The rule lives in the shared _classify, so promptfoo and JUnit comparisons with fewer assessed attempts also block. However, the acceptance tests cover only a trimmed copy of the recorded Inspect example and small synthetic Inspect logs, not real promptfoo or JUnit exports. Out of scope: comparing run-level configuration such as identity.epochs, handling duplicate IDs, detecting non-comparable runs, changing malformed-input messages (these inputs still exit 2), changing the GitHub Action (its outputs come from the same result), and any claim about upstream Inspect issue #5434. The controller's existing site checks (build_site.py and check_site.cjs) passed. Their log covers showcase pages at widths of 1440, 390 and 320 px and offline modes. They are regression checks of the existing site, not a visual or browser review of this feature's index.html diff report. No screenshots of that report were reviewed. It reuses the existing failed-row styling.
upgrade: Upgrade: install a release that contains commit d4a4afd. No data or configuration migration is needed. diff.json stays at schema evalarc.results-diff.v1 and gains one new kind value, less_covered. Any consumer that lists kinds explicitly should treat it as blocking. This change tightens the gate. A comparison where a check's assessed attempts fell used to exit 0 and now exits 1. If the gate starts failing, rerun the current evaluation with the same epochs and samples as the baseline, or review and commit a new baseline on purpose. Exit codes 0, 1 and 2 keep their meanings. Rollback: pin the previous version, which restores rate-only classification. Saved result files and existing report folders are unaffected in either direction.

title: score keyword lane classification against a labeled shortlist
summary:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes has a new --labels PATH option. It compares the keyword lane classifier with a hand-labeled JSON file. For each entry it scores title + '. ' + summary using ranked_lanes, whose top lane is the one distill.classify picks. It then applies the existing thin/ambiguous rules. Those rules now live in a flag_reasons helper that inspect() also calls.

The command prints a JSON report with:
- labels: the file's basename only
- labeled and margin
- agreement for all, confident (unflagged) and flagged entries, each as n, agree and rate (rate is null when n is 0)
- disagreements in input order, each with id (null when absent), title, label, predicted, reasons, best and runner_up

A disagreement with reasons [] is a confident misfile that the flags missed.

The whole file is validated before anything is scored. Invalid input exits 2 with one 'lanes: ' stderr line and empty stdout. This covers an unreadable file, invalid JSON or non-UTF-8 text, no items list, a non-object entry, an empty or non-string title or lane, a non-string id or summary, an unknown lane (the valid ids are listed), and combining --labels with --latest or --fail-on-suspicious. In labels mode the exit code is 0 whenever a report is printed. docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 9 documents the format and its limits.

The controller ran the checks, not me. In the pre-feature run, 8 of the 10 feature tests errored because argparse rejected --labels. On candidate c109acf the controller ran python -m pairadar --rerender --no-readme (exit 0), the 10 feature tests (all passed) and the full unittest suite (446 tests, OK).
usage:
Prerequisites: a checkout of this repository, Python 3.12 (the version in the controller's image), no extra packages. Run from the repository root.

1. List the valid lane ids:
python3 -c "from pairadar.config import load_config; print(', '.join(l['id'] for l in load_config().lanes))"

2. Create a SYNTHETIC sample file. The lane values are placeholders, not real human judgments. Replace them with your own labels:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
from pairadar.config import load_config
lanes = [l["id"] for l in load_config().lanes]
items = [
    {"id": "s1", "title": "Control barrier function safety filter with runtime monitor", "summary": "Synthetic example.", "lane": lanes[0]},
    {"title": "Untitled robotics note", "lane": lanes[-1]},
]
with open("my-labels.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    json.dump({"items": items}, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
EOF

3. Score it:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes --labels my-labels.json --margin 0.35

4. Read agreement.all.rate, then compare agreement.confident with agreement.flagged. Look first at disagreements whose reasons is [], because the flags missed those. Edit data/taxonomy.json and re-run on the same file to compare before and after.

5. Error example:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes --labels missing.json
This exits 2 and prints a single 'lanes: cannot read missing.json: ...' line.

Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_feature_5621e4c46330.py
limitations:
Scope:
- One input format (a JSON items list) and one entry point. --labels combines only with --margin.
- There is no threshold-based failure exit, CSV input, automatic taxonomy editing or model/provider call.
- Classification and scoring are unchanged.

What the numbers mean:
- Labels come from the user.
- The test fixtures and the usage sample are synthetic and labeled as such.
- The passing tests show that the counts, ordering and error handling match hand-computed expectations. They do not show broad classifier accuracy.
- Agreement on a small labeled set measures the current taxonomy on those items only. It is not general accuracy, and the margin is not calibrated.
- Keep the labeled set separate from the examples used to tune keywords.

Verification gaps:
- This is a CLI-only feature. No browser or visual review of it was done, and I did not check whether the full suite includes browser or showcase tests.
- An earlier review flagged unrelated banner SVG coordinate changes and a CHANGELOG file-list claim. The controller receipts do not include the final diff's file list, and I could not inspect it. So this text makes no claim about which files the commit touches beyond the lanes feature.
- The rerender check exiting 0 does not prove that assets are unchanged.
- Issue #73 is not addressed.
upgrade:
Additive. Without --labels, the existing command and its --latest, --margin and --fail-on-suspicious options keep their output and exit codes. The --latest default now resolves internally to the same radar/latest.json path. inspect() now calls the extracted flag_reasons helper, which uses the same rules. Label files are only read, and the feature adds no stored data or schema.

To roll back, revert the feature commit. Label files are user-owned and stay intact. Before releasing, confirm the commit's file list matches the lanes feature (see limitations).

title: choose the content gaps period and export the same window
summary:

After Show, the summary sentence, the gap table and the empty state cover the chosen window. The empty state names the window and suggests trying a longer period.

Download content gaps CSV exports the window shown on screen. Seven-day and 90-day files are named ai-chat-bedrock-content-gaps-7d-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.csv and ...-90d-.... A 30-day file, or one with a missing or rejected period, keeps the legacy name. The columns are unchanged.

The new AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::gap_window() accepts only an int, or a string of digits alone, equal to 7, 30 or 90. Anything else returns 30. The export handler reads the period only after the manage_options and nonce checks. The version is 1.48.0.

title: Decision coverage for recorded choices
summary: How often does a recorded choice component answer when it abstains below a confidence threshold, and how often is it wrong? EvalArc 0.16.0 chooses the threshold on calibration decisions, then reports coverage and selective error on held-out decisions. Invalid responses stay visible instead of being counted as wrong answers.
usage:
python -m pip install evalarc==0.16.0
evalarc decision-coverage RECORDS.json --max-error 0.2 --output runs/decision-review
# Open runs/decision-review/index.html; the release guide has a synthetic input example.
limitations: This reviews saved choice decisions only. The bundled example is synthetic and says nothing about a provider’s accuracy. Reported confidence is not calibrated by this command. The new HTML report passed structure and escaping tests; its layout and keyboard behavior were not checked in a real browser.
upgrade: Install EvalArc 0.16.0 to add this command. Reinstall 0.15.0 to roll back; existing inputs and generated reports are left alone.

title: Check a skill choice against the installed shortlist
summary: Skills Anywhere 0.16.0 adds a two-step route command. Prepare builds a shortlist of installed skills that can actually be opened; apply checks a saved choice against that shortlist before it is used. The result says whether the pick is selected, absent, below the confidence threshold, stale or invalid. The command does not load or run the skill.
usage:
npm install -g dsh-skills-anywhere@0.16.0
dsh-skills-anywhere route prepare "fill PDF forms" --json > request.json
# Save the recorded choice as response.json, then check it:
dsh-skills-anywhere route apply --request request.json --response response.json
limitations: The route command is CLI-only and checks installed skills on the current machine. Its default confidence threshold of 0.7 is a user-set cutoff, not evidence that any classifier is calibrated. Preparing or applying a route does not execute a skill or send it over the network.
upgrade: Install dsh-skills-anywhere 0.16.0 for the new route command. Reinstall 0.15.0 to roll back; saved request and response JSON files remain untouched.

title: stall-threshold sensitivity for recorded step-limit failures
summary: Adds --stall-sweep T1,T2,... to python -m robot_reel.stress. It re-labels verified recorded step-limit traces at up to eight stall thresholds in metres and reports per-threshold counts, changed and stable trials, and threshold-dependent boundaries against the unchanged 1 mm reference. No policy is re-run and no threshold is validated.
usage:
python3 -m robot_reel.stress docs/stress --reliability --stall-sweep 0.0005,0.002,0.005

The collection is verified first. Then the JSON output gains stall_sensitivity with these fields: schema, trials, reference_threshold_m (0.001), thresholds (sorted, reference included), by_threshold (counts and stalled_trials per threshold), changed (per non-reference threshold: trial, reference_kind, kind, tail_travel_m), step_limit_trials, stable_step_limit_trials, boundary (per step-limit trial: tail_travel_m, kinds per threshold, depends_on_threshold) and scope. Invalid input such as --stall-sweep=2 exits with status 2 and prints a message like: --stall-sweep value '2' exceeds 1 m; thresholds are metres of end-effector travel, not millimetres.
limitations: CLI-only; there is no UI change, so no browser or visual checks apply. The sweep describes label sensitivity on the recorded traces, using tail travel over the final tenth of frames as the only motion measure. It does not choose, calibrate or statistically test a threshold, and it does not re-run policies. The behavioral tests use labeled synthetic traces through the real CLI. For those tests, collection verification and loading are patched to stand in for a verified collection. A separate test checks the sweep's reference threshold against the sealed reliability.json of the published collection. The published reliability.json, the summary, the manifests and verify_site are unchanged. I did not run the tests in this environment.
upgrade: Upgrade to the release containing this change. The change adds one optional flag and one new output key, so existing commands, published packs and schemas keep working without migration. To roll back, revert the commit or reinstall the previous version. No stored artifact depends on stall_sensitivity.

title: report consecutive-failure streak and failing_since date for struggling sources in pairadar.health
summary: `python3 -m pairadar.health` now tells the maintainer and the nightly repair gate whether a struggling source has been continuously dark or is flapping. Each entry under `struggling` gains two fields next to the existing `source` and `failed_days`: `streak_days`, the number of consecutive runs (counted back from the latest run that recorded health inside the window) on which the source appears in `failed`, and `failing_since`, the `date` of the oldest run in that streak. A run on which the source answered, was served by its fallback endpoint, or was not attempted ends the streak. A new public helper `health.streak(runs, reference, window, source)` returns `(streak_days, failing_since)` and `(0, None)` when the source did not fail the latest run. All previously emitted keys (`reference`, `window_days`, `threshold_days`, `runs_with_health`, `failures`, `fallbacks`, and `source`/`failed_days` inside `struggling`), the worst-first ranking, the threshold and latest-run rules, and `--fail-on-struggling` exit codes are unchanged. The module docstring and docs/automation.md explain the two fields.
usage:
python3 -m pairadar.health --date 2026-09-27
# {
#   "reference": "2026-09-27",
#   "window_days": 14,
#   "threshold_days": 3,
#   "runs_with_health": 6,
#   "failures": {"ieee-spectrum": 5},
#   "fallbacks": {},
#   "struggling": [
#     {"source": "ieee-spectrum", "failed_days": 5, "streak_days": 5, "failing_since": "2026-09-23"}
#   ]
# }

# From Python:
from datetime import date
from pairadar import health
runs = health.load_runs()
print(health.streak(runs, date(2026, 9, 27), health.WINDOW, "ieee-spectrum"))  # (5, '2026-09-23')

# Tests:
python3 -m unittest tests.test_feature_644be79e9748
limitations: Streaks count consecutive runs that recorded health, not calendar days: if the publisher skipped a day, the gap is invisible and the streak continues across it. `failing_since` is bounded by the window, so an outage older than `--window` reports the oldest run inside the window (with `--window 3` a six-day outage shows `streak_days: 3`). Fallback-served runs are not failures and end the streak, matching the existing policy. No new CLI flags; fetch.py, the history.json schema, the repair job's trigger condition and `--fail-on-struggling` semantics are unchanged. Not covered: per-source item counts, feeds that answer but publish nothing, alerting, or the published site. Standard library only, Python 3.9+ as before (`from __future__ import annotations` is already in the module).
upgrade: Additive change to pairadar/health.py (one new function, two new fields per struggling entry, one docstring paragraph), one new test file tests/test_feature_644be79e9748.py, and three lines in docs/automation.md. radar/history.json is only read; no data files are rewritten. Upgrade by pulling the commit; consumers that parse the health JSON keep working because no existing key changes name or value. Rollback is `git revert` of the single commit, which removes the two fields, the helper and the test with no data loss.
